text:
Welcome to my office. I understand you are suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been persisting?

speaker: Doctor
text: I have received the initial lab results showing normal readings for stool ova and parasites, culture, and inflammatory markers. To narrow down the cause of your chronic diarrhea and abdominal discomfort, have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool, or do you experience significant weight loss recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your history of camping, the urgency of your bowel movements, and the feeling of incomplete evacuation, I am concerned about an infection or Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Can you describe the appearance of your stools, specifically looking for any blood, and do you have any family history of inflammatory bowel disease?

REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin
REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ulcerative Colitis. The clinical presentation of chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain relieved by defecation, urgency, and mucus is classic for this condition; the camping history suggests an infectious etiology but the four-month duration and inflammatory symptoms point toward IBD.
